about.nothing: EON DNS reports nothing anywhere. No account, no telemetry; the only things that leave this computer are the lookups themselves, encrypted, to the resolvers you chose, and the open lists it downloads.
about.title: About
bench.hint: Twelve real lookups to each resolver, from this connection. Takes a few seconds.
connect.hint.dns: Names are encrypted and filtered; the rest of your traffic goes as usual.
connect.hint.eon: All traffic goes to an EON tunnel server. EON runs none yet; set one in Settings.
connect.hint.native: Windows' own encrypted DNS is in use (Resolvers).
connect.hint.warp: All traffic goes through Cloudflare's free WARP network, sealed. Sites that are blocked by name open.
connect.hint.wireguard: All traffic goes to the WireGuard server you set in Settings.
connect.label: How to connect
diag.copied: Copied. It holds settings and counters, never a name you looked up.
diag.title: Diagnostics
dnssec.check: Also check DNSSEC on this computer (stricter; first lookups slower)
list.ads.hint: Advertising, analytics and tracking. Some sites may notice.
log.lede: The last 500 lookups, kept in memory only and gone when EON DNS stops. Off unless you switch it on.
log.name: Name
log.off: The log is off. Nothing about your lookups is being kept.
log.title: Lookups
mode.localhint: Encrypts, blocks, counts and checks signatures here. EON DNS stays running in the tray.
mode.nativehint: Windows encrypts lookups to one resolver and keeps doing so with EON DNS closed. No blocking or counters.
mode.title: How the computer uses EON DNS
nav.label: Sections
preset.adguard: Blocks ads and trackers itself; offers QUIC.
preset.cloudflare: Fast and widespread. Keeps no lookup logs, by its own audited policy.
preset.cloudflare-family: Cloudflare, blocking malware and adult content.
preset.google: Fast and widespread; keeps some logs for a short time.
preset.mullvad: Run by the VPN company; no logs.
preset.quad9: Non-profit, Swiss. Blocks known malicious domains.
problem.cancelled: Windows asked for permission to change the DNS settings and it was not given, so nothing changed.
problem.noeonserver: Set an EON server address in Settings first.
problem.noservice: The EON DNS service is not answering. Press the switch to set it up (Windows asks once).
problem.port: Something else is already answering DNS on this computer (port 53). Close it and try again.
problem.quit: EON DNS must put your DNS settings back before it closes, and permission was not given. It keeps running so the computer is not left without DNS.
problem.repair: Your DNS settings still point at EON DNS from last time, and they could not be put back. Turn protection on, or allow the repair when Windows asks.
problem.tunnelplatform: The tunnel is not available on this system yet.
problem.tunnelservice: The tunnel needs the EON DNS service, which has the rights to make one.
protection.lede: Blocking happens on this computer, from published open lists and your own rules. A blocked name is answered with nothing, so it fails at once instead of loading.
protection.title: What gets blocked
recent.logoff: Switch the log on (Log) to see names here. It stays in memory only.
recent.native: In Windows' own mode there is no blocking and nothing is counted.
recent.title: Recently blocked
resolvers.lede: Choose who answers. Several are asked at once and the first good answer wins. EON runs no resolver of its own.
resolvers.title: Where lookups go
ring.caption: The ring is the last hour, one tick a minute; amber is what was blocked.
route.off: Lookups go wherever your network sends them, readable on the way.
route.tunnel.after: , and names are answered by EON's resolver inside it.
route.tunnel.before: All your traffic goes sealed through
rules.allowhint: Wins over every list. Covers subdomains too.
rules.blockhint: Blocked whether or not a list has it.
settings.auto: Connect again when the computer starts
settings.title: Settings
settings.tray: Keep running in the tray when the window closes
setup.once: The first time, Windows asks once to set up the EON DNS service. After that the switch works instantly.
switch.label.off: EON DNS is off. Turn it on.
switch.label.on: EON DNS is on. Turn it off.
transport.title: Encryption
tunnel.eonhint: EON runs no tunnel server yet. When one exists, its address goes here.
tunnel.excludehint: One address or range per line, such as a game server or your office. Your home network is never tunnelled.
tunnel.saved: Saved. If the tunnel is on, it reconnected.
tunnel.title: Tunnel
tunnel.wireguardhint: Paste the file your own server or VPN provider gives you.
why.allowed: Allowed by your rule for {rule}, whatever the lists say.
why.label: Why is a name blocked, or not?
why.listed: Blocked: it is on the {list} list.
why.notrunning: EON's resolver is not running, so nothing is being blocked.
why.pass: Not blocked: it is answered by your resolvers.
